visual: Large vigorous deciduous shrub with oval green leaves turning vivid scarlet-red in autumn, followed by abundant bright rose-pink fruits that split open to reveal striking orange seeds.
water: Moderate while establishing; established plants tolerate some dry conditions.
soil: Moist but well-drained or well-drained soil; tolerant of chalk, clay, loam and sand and a wide range of pH.
soilWarning: Avoid permanently waterlogged soil and deep shade, which can reduce flowering, fruiting and autumn colour.
prune: Requires little routine pruning; remove dead, damaged or unwanted growth while dormant and lightly shape where necessary.
toxicity: Harmful if eaten to humans and pets; wear gloves when handling.
hardinessNote: −20 to −15°C · hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe.
resilience: Robust and cold-hardy; tolerates exposed positions and a broad range of soils once established.
uses: Autumn-interest shrub, specimen planting, wildlife gardens, informal hedging, mixed borders, screening.
